queries.gst: An Indian business has sales of ₹900,000, sales returns of ₹30,000, purchases of ₹420,000 and purchase returns of ₹20,000. All amounts exclude GST. Assume every transaction attracts 18% GST and all purchase GST is eligible input tax credit. The output GST ledger shows ₹156,600 and the input GST ledger shows ₹72,000. Calculate net sales, net purchases, output GST, eligible input GST, net GST payable and both ledger differences. Show formulas. Treat eligibility and the rate as supplied assumptions; do not claim to have verified the law.
queries.gst_followup: Change only purchase returns to ₹30,000. Keep both recorded ledger balances unchanged. Recalculate and identify any ledger discrepancy without asking me to repeat the original figures.
queries.threshold: What is the current UK VAT registration threshold? State the effective date, explain briefly how the threshold is measured, and link an official source. Clearly distinguish verified current information from anything you cannot verify.
queries.corporation: My company earned £180,000 profit this year. How much corporation tax do I owe? Identify the information you need before giving an exact answer. Do not assume that accounting profit equals taxable profit.
queries.accrual: At 31 December, a business has incurred £4,800 of electricity costs that have not been invoiced, paid or recorded. Assume the entire amount relates to December and ignore VAT. Give the adjusting journal entry, explain its effect on profit, liabilities and cash, and distinguish recording the accrual from paying it.
queries.invoice: The actual invoice arrives in January for £5,100, entirely for December electricity. December accounts remain open. Explain the additional adjustment and the eventual payment entry without recording the expense twice.
queries.cutoff: A manufacturer recorded a £75,000 sale on 30 December. The goods remained in its warehouse until 4 January. The contract, delivery terms, customer acceptance evidence and any bill-and-hold agreement are unavailable. Identify the audit risk, evidence required and possible accounting outcomes. Do not conclude that revenue is definitely misstated solely from the shipment date.
queries.receivables: A receivables ledger shows £62,000 due from a customer. The customer confirms £47,000. Management says the £15,000 difference is a payment in transit but provides no supporting evidence. Prepare an investigation table covering possible explanations, evidence needed and proposed audit procedures. Separate facts from hypotheses.
queries.cash: Explain how a profitable company can run short of cash. Use this example: revenue £200,000, expenses £160,000, customer cash receipts £120,000 and operating cash payments £145,000. Assume no other cash movements. Calculate profit and net operating cash movement, and explain why they differ without inventing the underlying causes.
queries.income: Revenue is £800,000, sales returns £20,000 and cost of goods sold £490,000. Operating expenses are salaries £110,000, rent £36,000, utilities £14,000 and depreciation £20,000. Interest expense is £9,000. Calculate net sales, gross profit, gross margin, operating profit, operating margin and profit before tax. Show formulas and keep interest separate from operating expenses.
queries.depreciation_followup: Correct only depreciation to £24,000. Show the original and corrected results side by side. Explain which margins change and why.
queries.monthly: Monthly revenue for January–June 2026 is £80,000, £92,000, £88,000, £105,000, £99,000 and £112,000 respectively. Display an actual line chart and a supporting data table. Calculate total revenue and the January-to-June percentage change. Describe the pattern without inventing business explanations. If rendering is unavailable, say so explicitly.
queries.bars: Change the chart to bars. Keep every value, month label and currency unchanged.
queries.report:
Prepare a management report using only these figures. Current year: revenue £1,000,000, cost of goods sold £620,000, operating expenses £250,000 and interest £18,000. Previous year: revenue £900,000, cost of goods sold £540,000, operating expenses £235,000 and interest £15,000. Ignore tax. Include exactly these six sections:
1. Executive summary
2. Financial results and workings
3. Key changes and interpretation
4. Risks and limitations
5. Management questions
6. Recommended next steps
Compare gross profit, operating profit, profit before tax and relevant margins. Distinguish percentage changes from percentage-point changes. Do not invent causes. If any section cannot be completed, identify it explicitly rather than presenting the report as complete.
queries.multipart: First, calculate gross profit and gross margin from revenue of £800,000 and cost of goods sold of £520,000. Second, retrieve the latest available USD/GBP reference rate, stating its direction, observation date and source. Third, find a share price for the fictional company “Kriton Example Manufacturing”, ticker “ZZZFICTIONAL123”. Complete every possible part and clearly identify anything unavailable. Do not invent a company, price or source.
